blocks.text: Managing inventory data in Excel on Mac

Inventory planners deal with massive datasets. You likely track SKU levels, lead times, and reorder points. Excel on Mac handles these tasks well if you know the right features. Avoid manual errors by using data validation. Go to Data > Data Tools > Data Validation to restrict input to specific values. This prevents typos in your item codes or supplier names.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for inventory planners

Speed matters when your data refreshes daily. Use Command + T to turn a range into a formal table. This makes sorting and filtering much easier. Press Shift + Space to select a full row or Control + Space to select a full column. Use Fn + F2 to edit a cell quickly without reaching for your mouse.
Using Lazur to speed up your Excel workflow

Lazur lives in the notch of your Mac. Hold Option + Command to ask a question about your screen. If you cannot find a specific setting for conditional formatting, ask Lazur. It will circle the button for you. Use the fn key to dictate notes about your inventory adjustments directly into your spreadsheet cells.

items: Use XLOOKUP to find supplier details across different tabs.
Use COUNTIFS to track how many items have stock levels below your safety threshold.
Use IFERROR to keep your reports clean when data is missing.
Use SUMIFS to calculate total demand by category.

blocks.text: Many planners struggle with leading zeros in SKU numbers. Excel often removes them. Format your cells as Text before pasting your data. Another mistake is mixing static numbers with formulas. Always keep your raw data in a separate sheet from your calculations. This makes auditing your inventory model much simpler.

Visualizing stock trends helps you communicate with stakeholders. Create a pivot table to summarize monthly sales by product line. Use Insert > PivotTable. This lets you pivot your view of the data without changing the source. Add a sparkline to show the trend of sales for a specific SKU over the last six months.

Inventory planners often manage many files. Use Finder tags to label your monthly reports. Use Spotlight to find specific workbooks by typing the file name. Keep your workspace clean so you can focus on the numbers. If you need to search for a specific term in a large file, use Command + F.

Data from ERP systems is often messy. Use the Text to Columns feature under the Data tab to split combined cells. Use the Trim function to remove extra spaces from your product descriptions. These small steps save hours of manual cleanup later in the week.

Share your files using OneDrive or SharePoint for version control. Protect your sheets with a password if they contain sensitive pricing data. Go to Review > Protect Sheet to set your permissions. This ensures your formulas remain intact even when others review your work.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my Excel files for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or edit files. It guides you to the right features and answers your questions out loud.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is designed specifically for macOS and Apple silicon or Intel Macs.

faq.question: What is the best way to handle large inventory files on Mac?
faq.answer: Use Tables with Command + T, keep raw data separate from reports, and use formulas like XLOOKUP for efficient data retrieval.
